\title{\boldmath Self-dual five-form invariants in ten dimensions:
a tensor--spinor correspondence, an exact rank certificate,
and an obstruction in the degree-ten stress flow}

\abstract{We study the ring of Lorentz invariants built from a self-dual
five-form $\Lam$ in ten dimensions, working in two presentations at once: the
tensor presentation in which $\Lam$ carries five antisymmetrised vector
indices, and the spinor presentation in which the same $126$ components sit in
the gamma-traceless symmetric square of a chiral spinor. We construct the
linear map between them explicitly and certify that it is invertible on the
selected chirality channel. Evaluating a family of $83$ candidate invariants
and computing the Jacobian of the resulting map in exact modular arithmetic,
we certify a rank of $81$ over the $126$ gamma-traceless coordinates, with an
explicit $81\times 81$ minor whose determinant is nonzero and is confirmed by
two independent determinant routines. We then turn to the stress-tensor flow
of the nonlinear chiral four-form theories of
Hutomo--Lechner--Sorokin. We prove, from algebraic self-duality alone and off
shell, that the free stress tensor of a self-dual five-form in ten dimensions
is traceless, so that the trace of the interacting tensor obeys
$\tr(\tau)[V_d] = 10(d-2)V_d$ and carries no quadratic part. This
tracelessness controls when the flow's trace generator becomes available, and
with it we compute the degree-ten seed closure exactly over the rationals:
$\dq\Aten = 14$, $\dq\Dten = 11$, and hence a three-dimensional quotient
$\dq\Qten = 3$ of degree-ten invariants that the seeded flow does not reach.
We state explicitly which of these results are proved, which are exactly
certified, and which hold only over the tested finite fields.}

\keywords{Chiral form fields, Duality in Gauge Field Theories,
Extended Supersymmetry, Differential and Algebraic Geometry}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}

A self-dual five-form in ten dimensions is an awkward object to write an
action for and an unusually rigid one to build invariants from. It is central
to type IIB supergravity, where the self-duality of $F_5$ is a constraint
rather than an equation of motion, and it is the highest-dimensional member of
the family of chiral $p$-forms in $D = 2p+2$ that includes the chiral two-form
of the M5-brane. Recent work has produced both a systematic account of the
invariants one can build from such a form \cite{Cederwall:2025invariants} and a
family of nonlinear chiral four-form theories in $D=10$ together with the
stress-tensor flows that connect them \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral}. The
four-dimensional member of this story is far better understood --- the
duality-invariant conformal extension of Maxwell's equations
\cite{Bandos:2020hgy} is an explicit closed-form theory --- and part of what
makes $D=10$ hard is that no comparable closed form is available.

This paper addresses three questions that sit between those two developments.

\paragraph{How many independent invariants are there, and can we certify it?}
The count of functionally independent invariants of a self-dual five-form is
available in the literature \cite{Cederwall:2025invariants}. What has been less
available is a certificate: an exact, reproducible object that establishes the
count without appealing to numerical rank estimates or to a tolerance. In
section \ref{sec:rank} we produce one. We evaluate $83$ candidate invariants,
compute the Jacobian of the resulting map exactly in modular arithmetic over
$126$ gamma-traceless coordinates, and exhibit an explicit $81\times81$ minor
with nonzero determinant, cross-checked by fraction-free Bareiss elimination
\cite{Bareiss:1968} and by Laplace expansion. The rank is $81$, and the
certificate says so in a form that can be re-verified independently.

We are not claiming the method. The workflow of enumerating candidate
contractions, evaluating them at sample points, and detecting relations from
the resulting Jacobian is due to Elamaran, Ferko and Scarlett
\cite{Elamaran:2025ml}; what we contribute here is its exact-arithmetic
execution for this particular five-form problem and the certificate that
execution produces.

\paragraph{Is the tensor presentation or the spinor presentation the right one?}
Both. The point of section \ref{sec:bridge} is that the choice is free, and
that this can be established rather than assumed. The space $\Lam^5_+V$ of
self-dual five-forms and the space $\Sym^2_{\gamma\text{-tr}}S_+$ of
gamma-traceless symmetric squares of a chiral spinor are both $126$-dimensional
in $D=10$; the isomorphism between them is classical and traces back to the
division-algebra structure of ten-dimensional spinors \cite{Kugo:1982bn}. We
construct the map $\Phi$ explicitly, verify that its forward rank is $126$ with
zero kernel on the selected channel, exhibit the exact round trip, and check
equivariance. The practical consequence is that a computation which is
expensive in one presentation may be moved to the other without a change of
content, and section \ref{sec:rank} uses exactly this.

\paragraph{What does the stress-tensor flow fail to reach?}
This is the question we regard as the most interesting, and section
\ref{sec:flow} is devoted to it. Given a seed interaction, the flow
$dV/d\lambda = f(T,\lambda)$ of \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} generates a
subspace of invariants at each degree. That subspace need not be everything.
At degree ten it is not: we find a three-dimensional quotient.

Establishing this required settling a question about the trace of the stress
tensor that turns out to have a clean answer. In section \ref{sec:trace} we
prove that the free stress tensor of a self-dual five-form in $D=10$ is
traceless identically and off shell, using nothing but algebraic
self-duality --- no equation of motion, no improvement term, no choice of
action formulation. The proof is three lines and rests on the observation that
a five-form has odd degree, so $F\wedge F = -F\wedge F$ and the full square
vanishes. The consequence is that
\begin{equation}
  \tr(\tau)[V_d] = 10(d-2)V_d ,
\end{equation}
which vanishes identically at $d=2$. A quadratic interaction therefore
contributes nothing to the trace, whatever its coefficient, and the trace
generator of the flow first becomes available at degree four. This is not a
technicality: section \ref{sec:counterfactual} records that if a quadratic
trace contribution were present, the degree-ten closure would grow from $11$
to $14$ and the quotient would collapse from $3$ to $0$. The tracelessness
lemma is the difference between an obstruction and no obstruction.

\paragraph{On exactness.} Every quantitative statement in this paper carries a
qualifier, and the qualifiers are not decorative. We write \emph{proved} for an
analytic argument, \emph{exactly certified} for a proof-producing exact
computation, and \emph{verified over the tested fields} for finite-field
evidence that has not been lifted to characteristic zero. Section
\ref{sec:limits} collects the statements that fall in the last category,
together with the results we deliberately do not claim. In particular we do not
convert modular evidence into a rational theorem anywhere, and where a rational
lift was attempted and failed --- as it did for $\tr(M^6)$, see section
\ref{sec:trm6} --- we report the failure rather than the guess.

\section{Setup and conventions}
\label{sec:setup}

We work in $D=10$ with mostly-plus signature and fix
\begin{equation}
  \eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-1,+1,\dots,+1), \qquad
  \varepsilon^{01\cdots 9} = -1 .
\end{equation}
For a $p$-form in $D$ dimensions with $t$ timelike directions the Hodge star
squares to
\begin{equation}
  \star\star = (-1)^{p(D-p)}(-1)^t .
  \label{eq:starsq}
\end{equation}
At $p=5$, $D=10$ this is $(-1)^{25}(-1)^t = (-1)^{1+t}$, so real self-duality
requires $t$ odd. Lorentzian $(1,9)$ and split $(5,5)$ signatures admit real
self-dual five-forms; Euclidean $(10,0)$ does not, and there the notion is
available only after complexification. We keep the real forms distinct
throughout, and the verification described in section \ref{sec:trace} tests all
three.

Let $\Lam$ denote the self-dual five-form, $\star\Lam = \Lam$. By
\emph{degree} we always mean homogeneous polynomial degree in the components of
$\Lam$, so $\Lam$ has degree one and any bilinear has degree two. Coupling
order is a different filtration and is not used.

The moment tensor and free stress tensor are
\begin{equation}
  M_{\mu\nu} = \Lam_{\mu\rho_1\rho_2\rho_3\rho_4}
               \Lam_{\nu}{}^{\rho_1\rho_2\rho_3\rho_4},
  \qquad
  T^{(0)}_{\mu\nu} = \frac{M_{\mu\nu}}{2\cdot 4!} .
  \label{eq:moment}
\end{equation}
We write $\tau = 48\,T$ for the $M$-normalised tensor; the factor is a
convention and nothing below depends on it.

In the formulation of \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral}, an interaction is specified by
a function $V(\Lam)$ and the Hilbert stress tensor is
\begin{equation}
  T_{\mu\nu}[V] = \frac{1}{2\cdot 4!}\Big(
      \Lam_{\mu}{}^{\rho(4)}\Lam_{\nu\rho(4)}
      - 25\, V_{\Lam\,\mu}{}^{\rho(4)} V_{\Lam\,\nu\rho(4)} \Big)
    - \frac{1}{4!}\, g_{\mu\nu}\Big( V - \tfrac12 \Lam\!\cdot\! V_\Lam \Big),
  \label{eq:hilbert}
\end{equation}
where $V_{\Lam\,\mu(5)} = \partial V/\partial \Lam^{\mu(5)}$ is
\emph{anti}-self-dual. That $V_\Lam$ has the opposite duality to $\Lam$ is the
one structural input beyond \eqref{eq:hilbert} that section \ref{sec:trace}
uses.

\subsection{The atlas of candidate invariants}

Candidate invariants are generated as contraction patterns, organised by an
associated graph and canonicalised so that patterns differing by a relabelling
are identified. Canonicalisation is performed with the exact algorithm of
McKay and Piperno \cite{McKay:2014}. We note that an earlier version of this
pipeline used a Weisfeiler--Leman refinement as a fallback, which was measured
to collide on precisely the graphs in play --- at order six, $49$ genuine
isomorphism classes collapse to $39$ refinement keys. Since the enumerator
retains the first graph per key, such collisions silently discard invariants.
The fallback has been removed; all results below use exact canonicalisation
only.

\section{The tensor--spinor bridge}
\label{sec:bridge}

\subsection{Statement}

Let $V$ be the ten-dimensional vector representation and $S_+$ a chiral spinor
of $\mathrm{Spin}(1,9)$, of real dimension $16$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \dim \Lam^5_+ V = \binom{10}{5}\Big/2 = 126,
  \qquad
  \dim \Sym^2_{\gamma\text{-tr}} S_+ = \binom{17}{2} - 10 = 126 ,
\end{equation}
the second because the symmetric square of a $16$-component chiral spinor has
dimension $136$ and the gamma-trace condition
$(\gamma^\mu)_{\alpha\beta}\Psi^{\alpha\beta} = 0$ removes ten. The map
\begin{equation}
  \Phi : \Lam^5_+ V \longrightarrow \Sym^2_{\gamma\text{-tr}} S_+,
  \qquad
  \Phi(\Lam)_{\alpha\beta}
   = \frac{1}{5!}\, \Lam_{\mu_1\cdots\mu_5}
     (\gamma^{\mu_1\cdots\mu_5})_{\alpha\beta}
  \label{eq:phi}
\end{equation}
is the standard one, built from the antisymmetrised product of five gamma
matrices, which is symmetric in $\alpha\beta$ on the chiral channel in $D=10$.

\subsection{What is certified}

The Clifford structure is extracted rather than assumed: the metric is read off
from the anticommutators of an explicitly constructed split oscillator
realisation, the Hodge square is computed per signature and compared against
\eqref{eq:starsq}, and the frame map is exact. Gate 1.1 of the verification
suite records $16/16$ checks passing on this structure.

For the bridge itself, gate 1.2 records $22/22$ checks: domain $126$, codomain
$126$, forward rank $126$, zero kernel on the selected chirality channel, an
exact round trip $\Phi^{-1}\circ\Phi = \mathrm{id}$, linearity under scaling,
and equivariance under the Lorentz action. The rank and kernel statements are
\emph{exactly certified}: they are computed in exact arithmetic, not estimated.

\begin{proposition}[Bridge invertibility]
\label{prop:bridge}
$\Phi$ as defined in \eqref{eq:phi} is a linear isomorphism
$\Lam^5_+V \to \Sym^2_{\gamma\text{-tr}}S_+$. Exactly certified: forward rank
$126$ with zero kernel, and the inverse verified by exact round trip.
\end{proposition}

\subsection{Why it is used}

The practical content of proposition \ref{prop:bridge} is that a polynomial
identity among invariants may be checked in whichever presentation is cheaper,
and the answer transfers. Gate 1.4 makes this precise degree by degree: at each
certified degree we record the tensor-side rank, the spinor-side rank, the rank
of the union, span equality in both directions, an explicitly fitted change of
basis, and validation on holdout samples not used in the fit. All $55$ checks
pass. Span equality in \emph{both} directions is the part that matters; one
inclusion is cheap and would not establish the correspondence.

\section{An exact rank certificate}
\label{sec:rank}

\subsection{The computation}

Following the enumerate--evaluate--relate workflow of \cite{Elamaran:2025ml},
we take $83$ candidate invariants, evaluate them at sample points, and study
the Jacobian
\begin{equation}
  J_{ij} = \frac{\partial \mathcal{I}_i}{\partial x_j},
  \qquad i = 1,\dots,83,\quad j = 1,\dots,126,
\end{equation}
where $x_j$ ranges over the $126$ gamma-traceless coordinates. The rank of $J$
at a generic point is the number of functionally independent invariants among
the candidates \cite{Zippel:1979,Schwartz:1980}.

Two departures from the standard practice are worth stating. First, the
Jacobian is computed \emph{analytically and exactly}: there are no finite
differences and no tolerance anywhere in the pipeline, so the rank is a rank
and not a thresholded singular-value count. Second, the computation is carried
out modulo a prime and repeated across a matrix of primes and sample seeds, so
that a single unlucky evaluation point or a single exceptional prime cannot
produce the answer on its own.

\subsection{What each cell reports}

The certificate is assembled from independent cells, one per (prime, seed)
pair, each run in its own process writing its own file. Every completed cell
reports the same accounting:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\toprule
candidates scheduled & $83$ \\
terminal status & $83$ evaluated, $0$ errors, $0$ interrupted, $0$ skipped \\
Euler homogeneity check & $83$ passed, $0$ failed \\
zero rows & none \\
coordinate dimension & $126$ \\
rank & $\mathbf{81}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The Euler homogeneity check is a falsification gate rather than a formality:
each candidate must satisfy $x\cdot\partial_x \mathcal{I} = d\,\mathcal{I}$ for
its declared degree $d$, which fails loudly if a candidate was mis-evaluated or
mis-graded.

The cumulative rank resolved by degree is identical in every completed cell:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrrrrr}
\toprule
degree & 4 & 6 & 8 & 10 & 12 \\
\midrule
cumulative rank & 1 & 3 & 9 & 21 & 81 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Degree twelve therefore contributes $60$ of the $81$. We record this because it
means degree-twelve data is load-bearing for the rank certificate even though,
as section \ref{sec:limits} explains, degree twelve is deliberately excluded
from this paper's central claims.

The matrix comprises fifteen cells: three sample seeds at each of three
fitting primes and three sample seeds at each of two holdout primes. All
fifteen report rank $81$, and all fifteen report the degree profile above.

\subsection{Pivot stability}

Agreement on the rank across cells is weaker than it first looks: two
computations can reach the same rank through different eliminations. We
therefore record which rows and columns the elimination selects as pivots in
each cell and compare them. Across all fifteen cells there are $81$ stable
pivot rows and $81$ stable pivot columns, with none unstable --- every cell
selects the same $81$ rows and the same $81$ columns. The certificate is
therefore reproducible at the level of the witnessing submatrix, not only at
the level of the answer.

\subsection{An exceptional class of primes}
\label{sec:badprimes}

One observation is worth reporting because it would otherwise cost a
reproducer a day. The bridge map $\Phi$ of section \ref{sec:bridge} has rank
$126$ at every prime we tested, but the duality channel it preserves depends on
the prime:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
primes & $p \bmod 8$ & $\mathrm{rank}(\text{SD}\cdot\Phi)$ & $\mathrm{rank}(\text{ASD}\cdot\Phi)$ \\
\midrule
$32713$; $32749$, $32717$, $32693$ & $1$, $5$ & $126$ & $0$ \\
$32719$ & $7$ & $126$ & $0$ \\
$32707$, $32771$ & $\mathbf{3}$ & $\mathbf{0}$ & $\mathbf{126}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

For $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ the two channels are exchanged: the subspace the
construction labels self-dual is precisely the kernel of $\Phi$. Note that
$p \bmod 4$ does not separate the cases --- $32719$ and $32707$ are both
$3 \bmod 4$ and behave differently --- so the rule is genuinely modulo eight.
Among the four classes, $p\equiv3$ is the one in which $-1$ and $2$ are both
quadratic non-residues. We have not traced the mechanism through the null-frame
Clifford construction, so we report this as \emph{observed} across seven
primes, deterministically, and not as a theorem.

The practical rule is to choose primes outside this class, which costs nothing.
We note that the implementation raises rather than substituting the working
channel when it meets such a prime; a silent substitution would assemble a
single certificate out of two conventions, and no downstream check would
notice.

\subsection{The minor}

Rank alone can be an artefact of elimination order. We therefore exhibit an
explicit $81\times 81$ submatrix and compute its determinant twice by
independent routines --- fraction-free Bareiss elimination \cite{Bareiss:1968}
and Laplace expansion --- requiring that they agree and that the result is
nonzero. They do, and it is.

\begin{theorem}[Rank certificate]
\label{thm:rank}
Over the $126$ gamma-traceless coordinates, the Jacobian of the $83$ candidate
invariants has rank $81$, exhibited by an explicit $81\times81$ minor with
nonzero determinant confirmed by two independent determinant computations.
Status: \emph{exactly certified} at each tested prime, across a complete
$15$-cell matrix of three fitting primes and two holdout primes with three
sample seeds each, with identical pivot selection in every cell.
\end{theorem}

The count $81$ itself is not ours; it is available in the source literature
\cite{Cederwall:2025invariants}. What theorem \ref{thm:rank} adds is the
certificate. We stress that the target value was at no point used as a
stopping condition: every cell evaluates all $83$ candidates and reports its
rank whatever that rank is, and agreement with the published count is a
validation of the pipeline rather than an instruction to it.

\section{The free stress tensor is traceless}
\label{sec:trace}

This section is self-contained and analytic.

\begin{lemma}[Vanishing full square]
\label{lem:square}
Let $F$ be a real five-form in $D=10$ with $\star F = \sigma F$, $\sigma =
\pm1$. Then $F_{\mu_1\cdots\mu_5}F^{\mu_1\cdots\mu_5} = 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For any $p$-forms, $\alpha \wedge \star\beta = \langle\alpha,\beta\rangle
\mathrm{vol}$. Taking $\alpha=\beta=F$ and using $\star F = \sigma F$,
\begin{equation}
  \langle F,F\rangle\, \mathrm{vol} = F\wedge\star F = \sigma\, (F\wedge F).
\end{equation}
But $F$ has odd degree five, and for a $p$-form
$F\wedge F = (-1)^{p^2} F\wedge F$; at $p=5$ this reads $F\wedge F = -F\wedge
F$, so $F\wedge F=0$ and hence $\langle F,F\rangle = 0$.
\end{proof}

Three features of lemma \ref{lem:square} are worth isolating. It is
\emph{off shell}: no equation of motion is used. It is \emph{algebraic}: only
antisymmetry and self-duality enter. And it is \emph{independent of $\sigma$},
so it applies equally to self-dual and anti-self-dual forms --- which is what
makes it strong enough for the next step.

\begin{theorem}[Tracelessness of the free stress tensor]
\label{thm:g10}
The free stress tensor \eqref{eq:moment} of a self-dual five-form in $D=10$
satisfies $\eta^{\mu\nu}T^{(0)}_{\mu\nu} = 0$ identically. Status:
\emph{proved}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\eta^{\mu\nu}M_{\mu\nu} = \Lam^{\nu\rho(4)}\Lam_{\nu\rho(4)}
= 4!\,\langle\Lam,\Lam\rangle = 0$ by lemma \ref{lem:square} with
$\sigma=+1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The interacting trace]
\label{prop:eulertrace}
For $V$ homogeneous of degree $d$ in $\Lam$,
$\tr(\tau)[V_d] = 10(d-2)V_d$, and in particular the trace vanishes
identically at $d=2$. Status: \emph{proved}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Tracing \eqref{eq:hilbert} with $g^{\mu\nu}$ in $D=10$ gives
\begin{equation}
  \tr T[V] = \frac{1}{48}\Big( 4!\,\langle\Lam,\Lam\rangle
    - 25\cdot 4!\, \langle V_\Lam, V_\Lam\rangle \Big)
    - \frac{10}{4!}\Big( V - \tfrac12 \Lam\!\cdot\! V_\Lam \Big).
\end{equation}
The first bilinear vanishes by lemma \ref{lem:square} with $\sigma=+1$. The
second vanishes by lemma \ref{lem:square} with $\sigma=-1$, since $V_\Lam$ is
anti-self-dual and the lemma never used the sign. Hence
$\tr T[V] = -(10/4!)(V - \tfrac12\Lam\cdot V_\Lam)$. For $V_d$ homogeneous of
degree $d$, Euler's theorem gives $\Lam\cdot V_{d,\Lam} = d\,V_d$, so
$\tr T[V_d] = (10/48)(d-2)V_d$, and in the $\tau = 48T$ normalisation
$\tr(\tau)[V_d] = 10(d-2)V_d$. The factor $(d-2)$ vanishes at $d=2$.
\end{proof}

Two independent facts are doing the work and both are needed: lemma
\ref{lem:square} removes the bilinear terms, and the Euler factor removes
degree two. Neither alone suffices.

\subsection{Independent verification}

Because proposition \ref{prop:eulertrace} carries the weight of section
\ref{sec:flow}, it was verified by a script that imports nothing from the
production code and rebuilds the Hodge star, the duality projection, the moment
tensor and the trace from the definitions in exact integer arithmetic. It
tests both signs of $\varepsilon$, both duality channels, and all three real
forms. The results:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
$\star\star$ on five-forms, Lorentzian $(1,9)$ & $+1$ \\
$\star\star$ on five-forms, split $(5,5)$ & $+1$ \\
$\star\star$ on five-forms, Euclidean $(10,0)$ & $-1$ \\
\midrule
samples tested & $192$ \\
samples with $\tr M \neq 0$ & $\mathbf{0}$ \\
samples with $M$ non-symmetric & $0$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The Euclidean row is a consistency check on \eqref{eq:starsq}, not a
counterexample: no real self-dual five-form exists there, and the verifier
skips the trace test accordingly.

Separately, the flow artifact was checked against the analytic formula
coefficient by coefficient. Every $\tr(\tau)$ target in the shipped system
carries coefficient exactly $10(d-2)$ --- $20$, $40$ and $60$ at degrees four,
six and eight --- and no degree-two target is present.

\subsection{Formulation independence}

Lemma \ref{lem:square} is a statement about an algebraically self-dual
five-form and nothing else, so it survives any reformulation preserving
$\star\Lam=\Lam$. The PST \cite{Pasti:1997gx}, clone and Hamiltonian
formulations differ from the one used here by terms proportional to the
auxiliary-field or PST-scalar equations and by field redefinitions; at the
order used these change $T_{\mu\nu}$ by such terms without introducing a
$\Lam$-bilinear trace, because any candidate bilinear is again
$\langle\Lam,\Lam\rangle$ or $\langle V_\Lam,V_\Lam\rangle$ and both vanish.
What is convention-dependent is the overall normalisation of $\tau$, not the
vanishing. A formulation containing a $\Lam$-bilinear that is not a full
contraction --- for instance one contracted through a background structure
other than $\eta$ --- would evade this argument; no formulation in the scope
considered here does so.

\section{The degree-ten stress flow}
\label{sec:flow}

\subsection{Three spaces that must not be conflated}

At degree ten there are several natural subspaces of the invariant space and
they have different dimensions. Distinguishing them is the substance of this
section; an earlier version of this analysis conflated the first and the
fourth and obtained a vacuous answer.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrr}
\toprule
object & dimension & quotient in $\Aten$ \\
\midrule
span of all $37$ degree-ten flow targets & 14 & 0 \\
new-forcing space ($\tr(\tau)$ excluded as a generator) & 5 & 9 \\
static stress span & 2 & 12 \\
\textbf{$\Dten$, the seed closure} & \textbf{11} & \textbf{3} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Only the last is $\Dten$. The first has no activation condition and therefore
reaches everything; the second removes $\tr(\tau)$ as a generator; the third is
static rather than dynamical.

\begin{definition}[Activation]
A flow target contributes to the closure only once every factor of its
coefficient monomial is already reachable. The closure $\Dten$ is the fixed
point of repeatedly adding targets whose activation condition is met, starting
from the seed set.
\end{definition}

This is where theorem \ref{thm:g10} enters. Because $\tr(\tau)$ has no
quadratic part, no degree-two $\tr(\tau)$ target exists, and nothing in the
$\tr(\tau)$ family is reachable until a degree-four direction is already in the
span. Without that, the family would activate immediately.

\subsection{The exact result}

The flow targets carry exact rational coordinates, so the fixed-point closure
can be run over $\Q$ with rational arithmetic rather than modulo a prime. This
matters for a reason worth spelling out: $\mathrm{rank}_{\F_p} \le
\mathrm{rank}_{\Q}$, and for a subspace that is \emph{subtracted} this
inequality points the wrong way. A $\Dten$ that were larger over $\Q$ than
modulo $p$ would make the obstruction \emph{smaller}, and agreement across
primes could not rule that out. Computing over $\Q$ removes the issue by
computing the rank rather than bounding it.

\begin{theorem}[Degree-ten seed closure]
\label{thm:d10}
Over the rationals,
\begin{equation}
  \dq\Aten = 14, \qquad \dq\Dten = 11, \qquad \dq\Qten = 3 .
\end{equation}
Status: \emph{proved}, with both bounds certified separately.
\end{theorem}

The upper bound on $\Aten$ needs no computation: the fourteen basis elements
\emph{are} the coordinate system, so nothing spanned by them exceeds fourteen,
and the modular rank supplies the matching lower bound. For $\Dten$ the
closure reached its fixed point in three sweeps, order-independently, and its
rank was read off by exact rational elimination. The lower bound is exhibited
by an explicit $11\times11$ minor with determinant
\begin{equation}
  12126533474468034240675840 \neq 0,
\end{equation}
computed by two independent routines that agree. The upper bound is
established separately by exhibiting three valid annihilators, which imply
$\dim \Dten \le 11$ directly. Because the two bounds are obtained by different
arguments, their agreement is evidence and not a tautology.

The three basis directions the seeded flow does not reach are $I_{10,6}$,
$I_{10,7}$ and $I_{10,12}$, corresponding to free columns $5$, $6$ and $11$;
the modular record agrees with the rational computation on both the rank and
the identity of the free columns.

\begin{remark}[Scope]
$\Dten$ is a \emph{seed} closure. The generator-extension problem
$dV/d\lambda = f(T,S,\lambda)$, in which additional generators are permitted,
is a different question and is not answered here. Nothing in theorem
\ref{thm:d10} should be read as addressing it.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The obstruction is load-bearing}
\label{sec:counterfactual}

A rule that nothing can violate is not being enforced. To check that the
activation semantics are doing real work, we insert the degree-two trace
contribution that theorem \ref{thm:g10} forbids --- a quadratic trace is
unconditional, so its coefficient monomial is empty and the $\tr(\tau)$ family
activates immediately --- and recompute:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrr}
\toprule
quantity & theorem \ref{thm:g10} holds & quadratic trace inserted \\
\midrule
$\dim \Dten$ & $\mathbf{11}$ & $14$ \\
$\dim \Qten$ & $\mathbf{3}$ & $\mathbf{0}$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

This is not a perturbation of the answer. It is the difference between an
obstruction and no obstruction, and it reproduces exactly the error made in an
earlier stage of this work, where taking the unconditional span of all raw
targets gave rank $14$ and quotient $0$ with nothing objecting at the time. If
the free stress tensor were not traceless, there would be no degree-ten
obstruction to report.

\subsection{Independent confirmation from the rational flow system}

The coefficient system for $dV/d\lambda = f(T,\lambda)$ was rationally
reconstructed through degree twelve, fit on five primes and validated on an
independent holdout. Its new-forcing span --- what the flow can create with the
homogeneity generator $\tr(\tau)$ excluded --- is:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lrrr}
\toprule
degree & full & new forcing & obstruction \\
\midrule
4 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\
6 & 2 & 1 & \textbf{1} \\
8 & 7 & 3 & 4 \\
10 & 14 & 5 & 9 \\
12 & 72 & 21 & 51 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

This uses a different script, a different algorithm, and rational rather than
modular arithmetic, and it recovers the same one-dimensional sextic
obstruction found independently at degree six. We record it as a cross-check,
not as a second proof of theorem \ref{thm:d10}: the quantity tabulated here is
the new-forcing span, not $\Dten$, and the two must not be identified.

\section{What is not established}
\label{sec:limits}

We regard this section as part of the result rather than an appendix to it.

\subsection{\texorpdfstring{$\tr(M^6)$ has no certified rational lift}
{Tr(M6) has no certified rational lift}}
\label{sec:trm6}

At degree twelve, the stress row associated with $\tr(M^6)$ was carried
through CRT lifting at fifteen primes, giving a modulus of approximately
$5.2\times10^{67}$. Twenty-nine of seventy-two columns still exceed the
uniqueness bound for rational reconstruction. The coefficients were therefore
\emph{not} guessed; $\tr(M^6)$ was adopted as a stress-adapted basis element
instead.

The contrast with the flow coefficients is the informative part. Those lifted
cleanly at five primes, while this single degree-twelve row remains unlifted at
fifteen. That pattern points to a genuine height problem specific to
$\tr(M^6)$ rather than to insufficient computation, which is why the natural
route forward is an analytic identity rather than more primes.

The four-dimensional \emph{rank} at this degree is certified. The
\emph{coordinates} are not, and no rational $\tr(M^6)$ coordinates appear
anywhere in this paper.

\subsection{Spaces certified only over the tested fields}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lcl}
\toprule
space & value & status \\
\midrule
$\Aten$ & 14 & proved over $\Q$ \\
$\Gten$ & 12 & proved over $\Q$ \\
$\Pten$ & 2 & proved over $\Q$ \\
$\Dten$ & 11 & proved over $\Q$ \\
$\Qten$ & 3 & proved over $\Q$ \\
$\Bten$ & 12 & \textbf{verified over the tested fields only} \\
$\Bten \cap \Pten$ & 1 & \textbf{verified over the tested fields only} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

$\Aten$, $\Gten$ and $\Pten$ are spans of distinct standard basis vectors in
atlas coordinates --- all fourteen, the twelve graph generators, and the two
lower products respectively. A set of $k$ distinct unit vectors has rank $k$
over any field, so their dimensions are structural and no prime can be
exceptional.

$\Bten$ is different. It is the span of the published equation-(4.24)
candidates, and each candidate's coordinate vector is \emph{recovered} by
solving a linear system against a design matrix modulo $p$, so the
coefficients are modular objects. We therefore have
$\dq\Bten \ge 12$ from the modular rank and $\dq\Bten \le 14$ from
$\Bten \subseteq \Aten$, and nothing between them is established. The
intersection $\Bten\cap\Pten$ inherits the gap through
$\dim(B\cap P) = \dim B + \dim P - \dim(B+P)$. Its modular value is $1$,
consistent across the tested primes, and that is exactly what we state.

Closing this would require a rational evaluator for the atlas elements, which
does not exist in the present package. The route is not exotic --- the
candidates' modular images at four primes give a CRT modulus of roughly
$10^{18}$, so a rational lift is unique when numerator and denominator are each
below about $10^9$ --- but whether the entries are that small is not known, and
it was not attempted here.

\subsection{Degree twelve}

Degree-twelve data is a certified \emph{input} to theorem \ref{thm:rank},
contributing $60$ of the $81$. It does not enter the title, the abstract or the
central claims of this paper, because doing so would require a complete atlas,
a verified product/primitive split, an exact rank certificate, a
trace/spinor comparison and holdout validation at that degree, and not all of
those are in hand. The scope decision is deliberate and is recorded as such.

\subsection{Claims we do not make}

We do not derive a correction to the type IIB effective action, and nothing
here should be read as one. We make no claim about causality, hyperbolicity,
supersymmetric completion or positivity of any theory in the family, because
none of those was calculated. We do not claim the enumerate--evaluate--relate
workflow, which is due to \cite{Elamaran:2025ml}. Novelty relative to the
existing literature is not asserted anywhere in this paper; a systematic
comparison against the relevant primary sources has not yet been carried out,
and until it has, no priority claim would be responsible.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The degree-ten quotient $\dq\Qten = 3$ says that a seeded stress-tensor flow in
the family of \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} does not reach every degree-ten
invariant of a self-dual five-form. Three directions --- $I_{10,6}$,
$I_{10,7}$, $I_{10,12}$ --- lie outside the closure. Whether they are reachable
once additional generators are admitted is the generator-extension problem, and
we have been careful not to answer it by accident.

The tracelessness result of section \ref{sec:trace} is the kind of statement
that is easy to assume and cheap to prove once asked, and the counterfactual in
section \ref{sec:counterfactual} shows the cost of assuming it wrongly. We
would flag it as the natural first thing to check when this analysis is
extended to the chiral two-form in $D=6$, where the analogue of lemma
\ref{lem:square} depends on $p=3$ being odd and so goes through, and to
$T\bar{T}$-like flows in higher dimensions more generally
\cite{Ferko:2024quv,Perry:1996mk}.

Two questions we would put to a reader with more context than we have. First:
is there a known analytic identity expressing $\tr(M^6)$ in terms of the atlas
generators? A single such identity removes the largest limitation recorded in
section \ref{sec:trm6}. Second: equation (2.36) of arXiv:2509.14351v2 prints a
trace sign that appears inconsistent with (2.33) and with the reproduced
$V(I_4)$ formula; we have not been able to determine which is intended, and our
implementation follows (2.33).

\section{The frame orientation, and how it was found}
\label{sec:orientation}

The bridge of section~\ref{sec:bridge} depends on a change of frame $L$
satisfying $L^{\mathsf T}\eta_{\text{null}}L=\eta_{\text{Lor}}$. That
congruence is solved modulo $p$, and the solve takes a modular square root.
A square root modulo $p$ has two values, $r$ and $p-r$; both give a valid
congruence, and they differ by a reversal of the frame's orientation.

Orientation is not cosmetic here. Reversing it reverses the sign of the volume
form, hence of the Hodge star, hence exchanges the star's $+1$ and $-1$
eigenspaces --- which is to say it exchanges which of the self-dual and
anti-self-dual five-forms the gamma map annihilates. Left unpinned, the bridge
realises the self-dual projector at some primes and the anti-self-dual
projector at others, with nothing to announce the difference until a later step
reports an image of dimension zero.

\paragraph{How it surfaced.} It surfaced through a holdout prime, which is what
holdout primes are for. Nine fitting cells and three holdout cells at
$p=32713$ completed normally; all three cells at $p=32707$ failed identically,
with the left-inverse construction reporting an image of dimension $0$ instead
of $126$. The bridge validation suite could not have caught this: it exercises
two primes, both of which happen to receive the orientation-preserving branch.

\paragraph{A wrong diagnosis, and why it was wrong.} The first explanation was
arithmetic: $32707$ is $3 \bmod 8$, the other tested primes were not, and a
second failing prime $32771$ is also $3 \bmod 8$. On two examples the pattern
looked like a congruence condition, and $32707$ was replaced by $32693$ as a
holdout while the matter was open.

That diagnosis is false. Once the orientation is pinned, $p=32633$ --- which is
$1 \bmod 8$ --- requires exactly the same branch as $32707$ and $32771$. A
prime outside the suspected class needs the identical correction, so the branch
requirement was never a function of the residue class. It was a coincidence of
the only two examples available when the rule was written.

\paragraph{The fix.} The construction now selects the branch under which the
self-dual space survives, in a fixed order, and this is a property of the
construction rather than a per-prime exception. Every residue class then works.
Table~\ref{tab:orientation} records eleven primes across all four usable
classes modulo $8$; all eleven land on the self-dual channel, and the three
that need the reversed branch are $32633$, $32707$ and $32771$ --- classes
$1$, $3$ and $3$.

\input{table_orientation}

\paragraph{Consequences.} Three, and the third is the reason this section
exists rather than a footnote.

First, $32707$ is restored to the holdout set and produces ordinary cells at
rank $81$. Nothing about it is exceptional. Second, $32693$ is retained as an
\emph{additional} validation prime rather than a substitute, and the assembly
step refuses a matrix that carries the substitute while missing the original,
since such a matrix has the right number of cells and passes every per-cell
check.

Third, every certificate in this paper was regenerated after the fix. The
recomputation was not expected to change any value, and it did not: at each
prime where the plain branch already survived, the pinned frame is
bit-identical to the unpinned one, and cells recomputed under the corrected
code agree with their predecessors in every candidate value, output hash,
Jacobian block and Euler check. The earlier numbers were right. They were
regenerated because a certificate should carry one evaluator's provenance
rather than two, which is a different requirement from being correct.

\section{Computational methodology}
\label{app:method}

\subsection{One writer per artifact}

Every scientific artifact in this work is produced by exactly one process. Each
computational cell runs in its own process, writes its own file, takes a lock,
and completes with an atomic rename. Each carries a unique execution
identifier, the hash of the frozen source it ran against, and hashes of the
candidate list and coordinate ordering it used. A cell that is interrupted
leaves a record saying so; a cell that completes leaves a terminal-status
record. Resumption skips completed cells rather than recomputing or, worse,
appending to them.

This discipline is not decorative. An earlier stage of this work ran six
concurrent test processes writing a single log, and the resulting file could
not be used as evidence for anything.

\subsection{Exact arithmetic throughout}

No result in this paper depends on a floating-point comparison or a tolerance.
Modular computations are exact in $\F_p$; rational computations use exact
rational arithmetic; determinants are computed by fraction-free elimination
\cite{Bareiss:1968} and cross-checked by Laplace expansion. Where a rational
lift from modular data is performed, it is validated on held-out primes that
were not used in the fit, and a lift that fails validation is reported as a
failure rather than retried until it passes.

\subsection{No stopping rules from published values}

No enumeration or rank computation in this work terminates because it reached a
published target. The values $81$, $14$, $11$ and $3$ appear in the literature
and are used here for validation only. Every cell evaluates its full candidate
list and reports whatever rank it finds.

\section{Conventions, and how they compare to the literature}
\label{app:conventions}

Sign conventions are the usual source of irreproducibility in this area, so we
record ours against the sources rather than leaving them implicit.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
quantity & this paper & note \\
\midrule
signature & $(-,+,\dots,+)$ & mostly plus \\
$\varepsilon^{01\cdots9}$ & $-1$ & fixes the sign of $\star$ \\
duality & $\star\Lam=\Lam$ & $\Lam$ self-dual \\
$V_\Lam$ duality & anti-self-dual & structural, used in prop.~\ref{prop:eulertrace} \\
$\Lam$ on shell & $\Lam_5=-F_5^+$ & identification of \cite{Hutomo:2025chiral} \\
degree & polynomial degree in $\Lam$ & \emph{not} coupling order \\
$\tau$ & $48\,T$ & the $M$-normalised tensor \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Nothing in section \ref{sec:trace} depends on the choice of
$\varepsilon^{01\cdots9}$: the independent verifier tests both signs and both
duality channels and finds the trace vanishing in all of them. The $48$ in the
definition of $\tau$ is a normalisation and propagates into the coefficient
$10(d-2)$; a different normalisation rescales that coefficient without moving
its zero, which is at $d=2$ regardless.

One discrepancy in the sources should be flagged. Equation (2.36) of
arXiv:2509.14351v2 prints a trace sign that we were unable to reconcile with
(2.33) of the same paper or with the reproduced $V(I_4)$ formula. Our
implementation follows (2.33). Readers reproducing this work who follow (2.36)
instead should expect a sign mismatch at that step, and we would welcome
clarification.

\section{Reproduction}
\label{app:repro}

The computational record is designed to be re-run rather than trusted.

\paragraph{What a reproduction has to produce.} Re-running the rank certificate
should yield, for every (prime, seed) cell independently: $83$ candidates
scheduled, $83$ evaluated, zero errors, zero interrupted, zero skipped, Euler
homogeneity $83/83$, no zero rows, coordinate dimension $126$, rank $81$, and
cumulative rank by degree $(1,3,9,21,81)$ at degrees $(4,6,8,10,12)$. A cell
that disagrees with any of these is a failed reproduction and should be
reported as one; none of these numbers is a tolerance.

\paragraph{Fitting and holdout.} The prime matrix separates fitting primes from
holdout primes. Rational lifts are fit on the former and validated on the
latter, and a lift that fails holdout validation is discarded rather than
refit until it passes. This matters most for the flow coefficient system of
section \ref{sec:flow}, where the lift succeeded, and for $\tr(M^6)$
(section \ref{sec:trm6}), where it did not and is reported as not having.

\paragraph{Choice of primes.} Every prime used must satisfy
$p \not\equiv 3 \pmod 8$, for the reason given in section \ref{sec:badprimes}.
A cell at such a prime does not produce a wrong answer; it fails to produce one
at all, which is the intended behaviour.

\paragraph{Determinism.} Sample points are drawn from seeded generators, and
the seed is recorded in each cell's output alongside the hash of the frozen
source, the candidate-list hash and the coordinate-ordering hash. Two runs with
the same seed and the same source hash must agree bit for bit; two runs with
different seeds must agree on every rank.

\paragraph{Independence of the degree-ten result.} Theorem \ref{thm:d10} is
reproduced by a verifier that shares no code with the production closure: it
recomputes the raw target span, the activated closure and the complete
invariant space from the flow artifact directly, checks order-independence
across sweeps, and certifies the lower and upper bounds by different arguments
(an explicit minor, and a set of annihilators). Agreement between the
production path and this verifier is the check we would want a referee to run
first.
